questions.questionText:
Statements:
"The private sector in India has shown remarkable resilience and innovation during global supply chain disruptions."
Conclusions:
I. The public sector has completely failed to show resilience during disruptions.
II. Private sector enterprises possess strategic agility and adaptive supply mechanisms.
questions.optionB: Both Conclusions I and II follow
questions.optionC: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
questions.optionD: Only Conclusion II follows
questions.explanation: The statement praises the private sector for resilience and innovation. It does not provide any comparison or negative remark regarding the public sector, so Conclusion I does not follow. Conclusion II directly interprets and explains what resilience and innovation in supply chain disruptions represent. Thus, only Conclusion II follows.

questions.questionText:
Statements:
"All successful software developers possess strong problem-solving abilities. Raj is a successful software developer."
Conclusions:
I. Raj possesses strong problem-solving abilities.
II. Anyone who possesses strong problem-solving abilities will definitely become a successful software developer.
questions.optionB: Only Conclusion II follows
questions.optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
questions.optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Conclusion I is a direct categorical deduction (Universal affirmative: All A are B, x is A => x is B). Conclusion II commits the fallacy of affirming the consequent (All A are B does not imply All B are A). Thus, only Conclusion I follows.

questions.questionText:
Statements:
"Company X has mandated that all employees complete a cybersecurity compliance training program by the end of the quarter."
Conclusions:
I. Company X places high priority on data protection and regulatory compliance.
II. Employees who fail to complete the training will be immediately terminated.
questions.optionB: Only Conclusion I follows
questions.optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
questions.optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Conclusion I is a direct and reasonable conclusion from mandating cybersecurity training company-wide. Conclusion II introduces an extreme and unstated punitive measure (immediate termination) not mentioned or implied by the statement. Hence, only Conclusion I follows.

questions.questionText:
Statements:
"Regular aerobic exercise significantly reduces the risk of cardiovascular morbidity in adults."
Conclusions:
I. Adults who do not engage in regular aerobic exercise will certainly suffer from cardiovascular disease.
II. Engaging in regular aerobic exercise is beneficial for maintaining heart health.
questions.optionB: Both Conclusions I and II follow
questions.optionC: Only Conclusion II follows
questions.optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Reducing risk does not imply certainty of disease in its absence; hence Conclusion I is invalid. Conclusion II is a valid and direct restatement of the health benefit. Thus, only Conclusion II follows.

questions.questionText:

Conclusions:

II. Country Z should immediately dismantle all renewable energy infrastructure.
questions.optionB: Both Conclusions I and II follow
questions.optionC: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
questions.optionD: Only Conclusion I follows
questions.explanation: The occurrence of outages despite heavy renewable investments proves that renewables alone were insufficient for peak winter demand (Conclusion I). Suggesting dismantling the infrastructure is an extreme, illogical reaction not supported by the premise. Hence, only Conclusion I follows.

questions.optionC: Both Conclusions I and II follow
questions.optionD: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
